title: Matinee Theater
paragraphs: CBS Sunday-afternoon dramatic anthology starring Victor Jory. OTRR documents the October 1944 retitling from Dangerously Yours to permit a broader range of stories.
The run breaks into several distinct periods: Matinee Theater title period (October 22, 1944 to April 8, 1945) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Richard Sanville (director), Mark Warnow (music director), Martin Gabel (performer, narrator, and host), Victor Jory (performer), Jean Holloway (radio adaptor and writer), Gertrude Warner (performer), and Betty Winkler (performer).
Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] and [[org|org.4798d1172deaae2c|Armed Forces Radio Service]].

The stories often return to literary and screen adaptation, romance and courtship, marriage, separation and reunion, classic literature on radio, historical and biographical drama, and radio preservation and collection metadata.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Dangerously Yours retitled Matinee Theater, Vicks-sponsored CBS Sunday anthology, Classic and contemporary stories adapted for radio, and Twenty-two of twenty-five historical programs represented in frozen broadcast set.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|columbia-workshop|Columbia Workshop]], [[show|dangerously-yours|Dangerously Yours]], [[show|x-minus-one|X Minus One]], [[show|the-chase|The Chase]], and [[show|the-mysterious-traveler|The Mysterious Traveler]].
